questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink alcohol quickly, it builds up in your body faster. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your system after one hour.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the road ahead.
Signal ahead.
Stop completely, then go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. You must come to a complete stop. Let other traffic and pedestrians pass. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on good pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then apply it again quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop. A locked rear wheel will not cause problems if your motorcycle stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:

options.text: First gear.
Neutral.
Third gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral.
questions.explanation: Start your motorcycle with the transmission in neutral. Most motorcycles have a light on the speedometer that shows when you are in neutral.

questions.question: In the center of a traffic lane, there is usually an oily strip. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Stay away from the oil and grease.
Not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay away from the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding on oil and grease buildup. This strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can often ride to the left or right of it and still stay in the center part of your lane.

questions.question: If you are passing parked cars on your right and no cars are coming toward you, ride:

options.text: On the left side of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic. This helps you avoid dangers like opening car doors and people walking between vehicles. If cars are coming toward you, stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: Alcohol reaches the brain ________ being consumed.

options.text: within minutes of
about an hour after
about two hours after

questions.correctAnswerText: within minutes of
questions.explanation: Alcohol reaches the brain and starts affecting your ability to ride within minutes of drinking. Driving or riding while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have more time to react to other drivers.
You have room to move safely.
You have few ways to escape.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have few ways to escape.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time to react and room to move. This provides many ways to escape danger, not few.

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move to the part of your lane where other drivers can see you best.
Move to the part of your lane closest to the traffic sign.
Move to the outside edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of your lane where other drivers can see you best.
questions.explanation: Move to the part of your lane that will make other drivers see you as soon as possible at a blind intersection.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may provide poor traction.

options.text: Pavement markings
Dry pavement
Pavement under a bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: Pavement markings
questions.explanation: Poor traction can occur on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel; lane markings; and metal covers like manhole covers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the right lane ends.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Ignore the stop line and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop line and then proceed through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, stop at the stop line first. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Ride within the posted speed limits.
Exceed the speed limit by up to 10 mph to complete the pass.
Pass more than one vehicle at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride within the posted speed limits.
questions.explanation: All passes must be done within legal speed limits. Pass only where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is usually most easily seen by other drivers when riding in which lane position?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: The center lane position is usually best when following a car. It places you in the driver's rearview mirror so they can see you. Always be ready to change positions if traffic or conditions change.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Accidentally move into another lane of traffic.
Get through the turn faster.
Keep control of their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accidentally move into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before turning or entering a curve.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a straightaway:

options.text: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straightaway, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: Where is the greatest potential for conflict between you and other vehicles?

options.text: At an intersection
On the highway
On any road

questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest potential for conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the tire locked until your next stop.
Continue squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake and then re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and then re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake pressure. Then re-apply the brake with controlled, gradual pressure.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn
No U-turn
No right turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They show specific traffic laws for that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If riding during the day, you should wear:

options.text: Clothing with reflective material.
A short-sleeved shirt.
Darkly-colored clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing with reflective material.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear clothing with reflective material to be more visible, even during the day. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: When someone passes you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed on your left, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the right side is dangerous. It may encourage the other driver to move back into your lane too quickly.

questions.question: When entering a turn, when should you change gears?

options.text: Before the turn.
During the turn.
Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A yellow traffic light warns you that the signal will soon turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: What is the best way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Turn on the radio.
Take frequent rest breaks.
Drink caffeine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent rest breaks.
questions.explanation: Take frequent rest breaks on long trips to reduce fatigue. Caffeine can make fatigue worse because you will feel very tired when it stops working. Wind, rain, and cold weather also increase fatigue. Dress warmly and use a windshield if you plan to ride long distances.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection carefully.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop completely and wait for a signal that lets you turn in the direction you want to go.
